# sustain_service (Resource)

Monitors grouped as one service, which is down by its rule and has one incident and alert for them.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "sustain_http_monitor" "api" {
  name   = "API"
  config = { url = "https://api.example.com/health" }
}

resource "sustain_service" "api" {
  name     = "API"
  monitors = [{ monitor_id = sustain_http_monitor.api.id, critical = true }]
}

resource "sustain_service" "shop" {
  name           = "Shop"
  description    = "What customers buy through."
  dependency_ids = [sustain_service.api.id]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String)

### Optional

- `at_least` (Number) For `at_least`: how many of its monitors down make it down; null otherwise.
- `client_id` (String) The client it is (docs/CLIENTS.md); null for a shared service.
- `contract` (Attributes) A client's contract, or a service's own: what its availability is held to in its reports, and how it's reckoned. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--contract))
- `critical` (Boolean) Whether it pages out of its client's support hours where a policy pages for critical services alone (docs/ALERT_ROUTING.md).
- `dependency_ids` (List of String) The services it depends on, by id (docs/SERVICES.md). Sustain's `depends_on`, a name Terraform keeps for its own.
- `description` (String)
- `down_when` (String) Down when any of its monitors is, every one is, at least `at_least` are, or a critical one is.
- `manual_status` (String) The status set by hand; null for `automatic`.
- `monitors` (Attributes List) Its monitors now, in the order they joined. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--monitors))
- `one_incident` (Boolean) Whether, while it's down, its monitors' outages join its one incident and alert once.
- `show_monitors` (Boolean) Whether its row on the status page opens to show its public monitors.
- `status_mode` (String) How it's shown: by its monitors and what it depends on (automatic), as set by hand (manual), or as set unless those say worse (hybrid).
- `status_page_visibility` (String) Whether a monitor is shown on the status page.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) An ISO 8601 time in UTC.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

<a id="nestedatt--contract"></a>
### Nested Schema for `contract`

Required:

- `maintenance` (String) Whether maintenance is left out of its time, or counted as downtime.

Optional:

- `hours` (Attributes) A client's support hours: on these days, from and to these times of day, by a time zone's clocks, within the day. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--contract--hours))
- `target_percent` (Number) The availability it promises, a percentage above 0 and up to 100, such as 99.9; null for none.

<a id="nestedatt--contract--hours"></a>
### Nested Schema for `contract.hours`

Required:

- `days` (List of String) In the week's order, once each.
- `end_time` (String) When they end, after they begin, on the same day: "24:00" at the latest.
- `start_time` (String) When they begin, as "09:00".
- `time_zone` (String) The IANA time zone whose clocks they keep, as Europe/London.



<a id="nestedatt--monitors"></a>
### Nested Schema for `monitors`

Required:

- `monitor_id` (String)

Optional:

- `critical` (Boolean) Whether the service is down whenever this monitor is, by the `critical` rule.

Read-Only:

- `joined_at` (String) An ISO 8601 time in UTC.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# By its id in Sustain, as its page in the console, or its API, gives it.
terraform import sustain_service.shop <id>
```
